title: Oil Seal
model_title: Radial Shaft Oil Seal (Lip Seal with Garter Spring & Dust Lip)

introduction.definition: A radial oil seal (lip seal) keeps lubricant inside a housing and dirt outside. An elastomer lip, moulded slightly smaller than the shaft and loaded by a garter spring, runs on a smooth, hard shaft surface with a thin oil film; its asymmetric shape pumps oil back toward the oil side. A dust lip faces outward.
applications: Gearboxes, motors and pump bearing housings
Vehicle axles, hydraulic motors and general machinery
key_points: Install with the lip toward the oil

pressure.title: Narrow, controlled lip contact
pressure.description: The lip is moulded slightly smaller than the shaft (interference) and the garter spring adds radial load, so it contacts the shaft over a band only ≈ 0.1–0.3 mm wide. A thin oil film under the lip lubricates it; the asymmetric lip angles (steeper on the oil side) create a pumping action that returns oil. Lip seals suit low pressure (≈ ≤ 0.5 bar) and surface speeds up to about 10–30 m/s depending on the elastomer; the dust lip keeps dirt out.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Oil Seal.
Check for weeping / oil drips.
Check shaft for grooving when seals are replaced.
Replace seal; use wear sleeve if shaft is grooved.
Watch for leakage: oil at the shaft. Common cause: hardened lip (heat).
Watch for lip wear: short life. Common cause: dry running, abrasive dirt, rough shaft.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
